A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same divergence-based alignment framework and KLDO method. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite added sections and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian simulations, model-alignment benchmark results, separation analyses and example model outputs in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulations, benchmark results and appendix analyses, and additionally reports average ranks for the existing comparisons.

M1.justification: The KLDO objective, gradient estimation with a moving-average denominator, FDO formulation and alignment procedures are unchanged. The corrected divergence identity does not alter the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SafeAligner/Alpaca-derived CR and preference data, AdvBench clean/GCG scenarios, SALAD, ToxiGen, AlpacaEval, MMLU and GSM8K-CoT. No additional evaluated task or population appears.

E2.justification: DPO, KTO and BCO remain the evaluated alignment comparators against KLDO. Base-model participation and comparator membership within the main and appendix comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.2.2 and Table 2 add average rank as an evaluation summary. Existing datasets, model configurations, training budgets and testing procedures are retained; the PDFs do not establish experimental reruns.

E4.justification: The CR-versus-preference comparison, separation–robustness correlation, PCA variance analysis and example responses are retained. The added rank column summarizes existing comparisons without adding an ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains identical correlations and p-values, and the AlpacaEval plot retains its existing error bars. The new checklist adds no run counts, seeds or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds average-rank results: KLDO scores 1.6 for Llama3.2-1B, tied with BCO, and 1.4 for the other four models. Existing benchmark values, correlations, plotted results and appendix outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 changes the minus sign before the Q-expectation of ln(1−T) to a plus in Equation 8 and the JS derivation in Lemma B.1. This corrects a mathematical inconsistency; the remaining definitions, theorems and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged. The revised introduction and new conclusion retain the same central contributions: divergence estimation, KLDO/FDO, alignment consistency, CR-induced separation and its relationship to robustness.

C2.justification: v3 interprets average rank as consistent robustness and newly asserts that KLDO has the highest overall robustness score across all models. That assertion conflicts with Table 2: Mistral BCO scores 96.29 versus KLDO's 87.87. The limitations also add factual consistency as a prospective application.

D1.justification: v3 specifies min–max normalization to [0,1] followed by averaging for the existing overall robustness score, where v2 only described a standardized weighted average. Appendix C's training details, hardware and code/data links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited research works and related-work discussion are unchanged. The new conclusion reiterates the existing positioning of divergence estimation as a unifying explanation and basis for alignment objectives.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the introduction and contribution list, edits robustness and limitations prose, and adds a conclusion, acknowledgments and NeurIPS checklist. The existing technical exposition and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds explanatory Figures 2–3 and an average-rank column in Table 2, with revised captions, sizing and float placement. Existing plot images are retained and renumbered. Pagination also leaves the covariance definition isolated on an otherwise nearly empty page 29.

improvement.justification: The corrected JS identity and proof, explanatory Figures 2–3 and dedicated conclusion modestly improve mathematical consistency and accessibility. Experimental validation is otherwise unchanged. These gains are tempered by the new, incorrect claim of highest overall robustness across every model: Table 2 still favors BCO over KLDO on Mistral.
